lines.text: Everyone who lives in the Netherlands must pay tax [belasting].
With that money the government pays for things that are important for everyone: roads, dikes [dijken], the police, schools, benefits and hospitals.
The municipality uses it to pay for, for example, the library, the swimming pool, youth care, social assistance and courses for refugees [vluchtelingen].
Income tax [Inkomstenbelasting]: you pay tax on part of your income.
On your payslip [loonstrook] you see your net income [netto-inkomen] and gross income [bruto-inkomen].
If you do not earn very much, you pay no or very little income tax.
You pay municipal taxes [gemeentelijke belastingen] separately to the municipality, for example property tax [onroerendezaakbelasting (OZB)] for people who own their home.
With a low income you can often get a discount [korting] or a waiver [kwijtschelding] — with a waiver you do not have to pay anything.
You must apply for this first; the municipality then assesses [beoordeelt] how much you have to pay.
Filing a tax return [Aangifte doen bij de Belastingdienst]: if you have an income, you must file a return every year.
For people in salaried employment [loondienst] the Belastingdienst already knows how much they earned; entrepreneurs [ondernemers] must report their income themselves.
You first receive a tax return letter [aangiftebrief].
Then you file your return via internet or an app — logging in with your DigiD on Mijn Belastingdienst.
Sometimes you have to pay extra tax; sometimes you get money back, for example if you paid too much or had extra costs for study [studie], your own home or your children.
Allowances [Toeslagen]: an allowance is money you receive from the Belastingdienst for costs you incur.
There are three allowances:
Rent allowance [Huurtoeslag] — for the rent you pay.
Healthcare allowance [Zorgtoeslag] — for your health insurance.
Childcare allowance [Kinderopvangtoeslag] — for childcare [kinderopvang] (which is not the same as child benefit [kinderbijslag]).
You can apply for an allowance if you have a low income, via Mijn Toeslagen (with DigiD) or the Toeslagen app.
If your situation changes (higher salary, moving, getting married or living together), you must report this — otherwise you may have to pay back [terugbetalen] a lot of money later.
You can get help with your return from someone you know, at the Belastingdienst itself and at many libraries.
If you disagree with the Belastingdienst, you can file an objection [bezwaar].
If you have to pay a lot of money, you can make an arrangement to pay in instalments [termijnen].
